title: Scheme tests and permanence of quasi-separated algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Regard schemes as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Use the algebraic-space predicates of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]: a space is quasi-compact if it has a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], a morphism $a:A\to B$ is quasi-compact if $A\times_BC$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact algebraic space $C\to B$, and $a$ is quasi-separated if $\Delta_a:A\to A\times_BA$ is quasi-compact. Separated means that every scheme base change of $\Delta_a$ is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For any morphism $a:A\to B$, $a$ is quasi-separated if and only if for every scheme $T$ and map $T\to B$, the algebraic-space morphism $A\times_BT\to T$ is quasi-separated. If $a$ is quasi-separated, then for every algebraic-space morphism $B'\to B$, its base change $A\times_BB'\to B'$ is quasi-separated. If $a:A\to B$ and $b:B\to C$ are quasi-separated morphisms of algebraic spaces, then $b\circ a$ is quasi-separated. Every separated morphism of algebraic spaces is quasi-separated. No finiteness, quasi-compactness, or absolute separation assumption is imposed on $S,A,B,C,B'$ or on the morphisms.

source.place: Tags 03KM (lemma-separated-local), (1) iff (2), for the quasi-separated axiom; 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), quasi-separated axiom; 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), quasi-separated axiom; 03KK (lemma-trivial-implications), separated implies quasi-separated.

proof.text: First record the elementary all-test quasi-compactness calculus. If $f:X\to Y$ is quasi-compact and $Y\prime\to Y$ is arbitrary, then for every quasi-compact space $Z\to Y\prime$ the source of the tested base change is $X\times_YZ$, which is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $f$. If $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ are quasi-compact, then for any quasi-compact $W\to Z$, first $Y_W$ is quasi-compact, and then $X\times_YY_W\cong X\times_ZW$ is quasi-compact. These identifications follow from the sheaf fibre-product universal property. Thus quasi-compact morphisms are preserved by base change and composition, for exactly the all-algebraic-space-test definition used here.

source.place: Tags 03HE (definition-quasi-compact), 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact), 03HG (lemma-composition-quasi-compact); the omitted transitivity arguments are written out

proof.text: Put $D=A\times_BA$. For $A\prime=A\times_BB\prime$, the diagonal $\Delta_{A\prime/B\prime}$ is the pullback of $\Delta_a$ along $A\prime\times_{B\prime}A\prime\to D$: a section of either pullback is a single section of $A$ with the prescribed equal pair and the prescribed $B\prime$-coordinate. For $a:A\to B$, $b:B\to C$, there is a factorization $\Delta_{ba}=j\circ\Delta_a$ with $j:D\to A\times_CA$. The square with bottom arrow $\Delta_b:B\to B\times_CB$ and right arrow $(a,a):A\times_CA\to B\times_CB$ is cartesian: its sections are pairs $(x_1,x_2)$ with $a(x_1)=a(x_2)$, precisely sections of $D$. These descriptions commute with restriction to every test scheme and hence give the asserted sheaf identities.

source.place: Tags 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), 03KN (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), and 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated): the two diagonal identities

proof.text: If $a$ is quasi-separated, $\Delta_a$ is quasi-compact. The pullback identity of step 2 and base-change calculus of step 1 make $\Delta_{A\prime/B\prime}$ quasi-compact, proving arbitrary algebraic-space base-change stability. In particular every scheme base change is quasi-separated. If $a,b$ are quasi-separated, $\Delta_a,\Delta_b$ are quasi-compact; the cartesian square of step 2 makes $j$ quasi-compact and step 1 makes $j\Delta_a=\Delta_{ba}$ quasi-compact. By the definition this proves composition stability.

source.place: Tags 03KL and 03KQ, quasi-separated clauses; Tag 03KM (lemma-separated-local), (1) implies (2)

proof.text: Conversely assume every scheme base change of $a$ is quasi-separated. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $p:T\to D=A\times_BA$. Write its two coordinates as $x_1,x_2:T\to A$, and give $T$ the common map $ax_1=ax_2$ to $B$. Put $A_T=A\times_BT$. The two sections $(x_1,\mathrm{id}_T),(x_2,\mathrm{id}_T)$ define $s:T\to A_T\times_TA_T$. The pullback of $\Delta_{A_T/T}$ along $s$ is $A\times_DT\to T$: on any scheme over $T$, both fibre products impose precisely $x=x_1=x_2$. The hypothesis makes $\Delta_{A_T/T}$ quasi-compact, so step 1 makes this pullback quasi-compact. Apply quasi-compactness descent to $\Delta_a$ and the singleton family $\{p\}$. This is a small jointly surjective family; its map is flat and locally of finite presentation on scheme charts because it is representable etale and scheme etale maps have these properties by definition. The descent theorem therefore makes $\Delta_a$ quasi-compact. This proves the reverse scheme-test implication without any quasi-compactness requirement on $T$ or $D$.

source.place: Tag 03KM (lemma-separated-local), (2) implies (1), expanded by the atlas test for the diagonal; Tag 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), etale descent

proof.text: Finally suppose $a$ is separated. For an arbitrary quasi-compact algebraic space $Z\to D$, choose its representable surjective etale atlas $U\to Z$ with $U$ a quasi-compact scheme, as in the definition. By separatedness, $E=A\times_DU\to U$ is a closed immersion of schemes. The affine characterization of a closed immersion says that the inverse image of an affine open is affine; it is therefore quasi-compact by the affine-scheme lemma. Thus $E\to U$ is quasi-compact as a scheme morphism, and the quasi-compact inverse-image lemma applied to the quasi-compact open $U$ itself shows that $E$ is a quasi-compact scheme. The map $E\to A\times_DZ$ is representable surjective etale, being the pullback of $U\to Z$. It is consequently a quasi-compact scheme atlas of $A\times_DZ$. Since $Z$ was any quasi-compact space test, $\Delta_a$ is quasi-compact in the all-test sense, and $a$ is quasi-separated.
